name: Antichain Number
definition: An **antichain teacher mapping** for a finite binary class $\mathcal H$ assigns every $h\in\mathcal H$ a labeled sample $T(h)$ consistent with $h$, such that for distinct $h,g\in\mathcal H$ neither $T(h)\subseteq T(g)$ nor $T(g)\subseteq T(h)$. The **antichain number** $\mathrm{AN}(\mathcal H)$ is the minimum, over such mappings, of $\max_{h\in\mathcal H}|T(h)|$.
graph_summary: Smallest maximum sample size in a consistent teaching map whose assigned samples are inclusion-incomparable.
description: A batch-teaching parameter based on antichain mappings of labeled samples.
origin_references: The antichain number is defined and studied in \cite{simon2023map}; its VC upper bound is attributed there to \cite{mansouri2022batch}.

symmetric.proof: Complementing every concept and every label in an assigned sample preserves sample consistency, sample cardinality, and inclusion between samples, hence preserves antichain teacher mappings.
